items.label: section_header
items.text: UNITS OF VOLUME

items.label: text
items.text: Volumes (of gases or liquids) are measured in

items.label: text
items.text: or cubic centimetres (cm³)

items.label: text
items.text: cubic decimetres (dm³)

items.label: text
items.text: or litres (l)

items.label: text
items.text: 1litre = 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³

items.label: text
items.text: The most important thing you need to be able to do is to convert between cm³ and dm³. Figure 6.3 shows how you can do this.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 6.3 Because 1 dm³ is equivalent to 1000 cm3, to convert dm³ to cm³ we have to go from 1 to 1000, therefore we need to multiply by 1000. To convert cm³ to dm³ we need to go from 1000 down to 1, therefore we divide by 1000.

items.label: section_header
items.text: THE VOLUME OCCUPIED BY 1 MOLE OF A GAS

items.label: text
items.text: 1 mole of any gas contains the same number of molecules and so occupies the same volume as 1 mole of any other gas at the same temperature and pressure.

items.label: text
items.text: At room temperature and pressure, the volume occupied by 1 mole of any gas is approximately 24 dm³ (24 000 cm³). The volume occupied by 1 mole of a gas is often called the molar volume.

items.label: text
items.text: You can use the triangles shown in Figures 6.4 and 6.5 to convert between volumes and numbers of moles.

items.label: text
items.text: The abbreviation rtp is commonly used for 'room temperature and pressure'. rtp is usually taken as 20–25 °C and 1 atmosphere pressure.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXTENSION WORK

items.label: text
items.text: To be absolutely 100% correct, the molar volume has units of dm³/mol or cm³/mol. At International GCSE you are unlikely to encounter this unit.

items.label: section_header
items.text: CALCULATIONS WITH MOLAR VOLUME

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate the volume in dm³ of 0.20 mol CO2 at rtp:

items.label: text
items.text: volume = number of moles × molar volume

items.label: text
items.text: Because we want the volume in dm³ we use 24 dm³ as the molar volume:

items.label: text
items.text: volume = 0.20×24 =4.8dm³
